chunks: They said: 'We took you to be an evil omen, and those with you.' He replied: 'Your omen is with Allah; rather, you are a people being tested.'

key_terms.اطَّيَّرْنَا: We took to be an omen (usually evil)
key_terms.طَائِرُكُمْ: Your omen / Your bird of ill omen

ai.seo_question: What did Prophet Saleh say in response to his people calling him a bad omen?
ai.summary: In this verse, Prophet Saleh (AS) refutes the superstition of his people, who attributed misfortune to him and his followers, asserting that true 'bad omen' (tayyarah) is from Allah alone. Shia scholars highlight this as a correction of pre-Islamic Jahiliyyah beliefs, emphasizing that trials (fitnah) are divine tests rather than inherent curses. This dialogue underscores the theological principle that misfortune is not tied to the righteous but is a consequence of one's own spiritual state and divine decree.
